subtopics.title: Mean, Median and Mode for Ungrouped Data

questions.question: For the homework times 12, 14, 15, 15, 18, 21, 23, 25, 28 (sum 171), the mean is:
The median of those nine ordered values is:
options: $18$ — the fifth value, with four below and four above

questions.question: Before finding a median you must always:
options: Order the data from smallest to largest

questions.question: The mode of the dataset is 15 because:
options: It is closest to the mean
It sits in the middle of the list
It appears more often than any other value

subtopics.title: Outliers and Choosing the Right Measure

questions.question: Adding the outlier 120 to the nine times changes the mean to:
With ten values, the median becomes:
options: $\dfrac{18 + 21}{2} = 19{,}5$ — the mean of the two middle values

questions.question: For suburb house prices that include one 20-million-rand mansion, the best measure of the typical price is:
options: The mean, because it uses every value
The median, because it is not affected by the extreme value that drags the mean upward
The mode, because prices repeat often

questions.question: A shoe-shop manager ordering stock cares most about the:
options: Mode — the size most customers actually wear

subtopics.title: Grouped Data and the Estimated Mean

questions.question: The midpoint of the class interval from 30 up to below 40 is:
For the 40 test marks with frequencies 4, 6, 11, 12, 7 and midpoints 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, the estimated mean is:
The grouped mean is only an ESTIMATE because:
options: The table hides the exact values, so each learner is assumed to sit at the interval midpoint

subtopics.title: Modal Interval, Median Interval and Reading the Table

questions.question: With frequencies 4, 6, 11, 12, 7, the modal interval is:
options: $60$ up to below $70$ — the class with the highest frequency

questions.question: The cumulative frequencies run 4, 10, 21, 33, 40. The 20th and 21st values, and hence the median interval, lie in:
options: $50$ up to below $60$ — the running total passes from 10 to 21 there

questions.question: The estimated mean of 58 lies below the modal interval because:
options: The low-mark tail of the data drags the mean down while the mode ignores it
The mean is always smaller than the mode

questions.question: A learner answers 'the modal interval is 12'. The error is:
options: The mode of grouped data must be a midpoint
12 is the frequency; the answer must name the interval, 60 up to below 70

questions.question: In the three pictures, the MEAN is the:
options: Middle person in the ordered line
Value with the most hands raised
Pot — pour every value together and share it out equally

questions.question: The median is found by:
options: Ordering the values and taking the middle position

questions.question: The measure that only ever uses counting — never adding or dividing — is the:
When the 120-minute learner joins, the median barely moves because:
options: The median only depends on the middle POSITION of the ordered line, not on how extreme the end values are
The median is recalculated with the outlier removed

questions.question: After the outlier joins, nine of the ten learners sit below the new mean of 29,1. This shows that:
options: The mean is now more accurate
An outlier can drag the mean until it describes almost nobody
The mode should have increased too

questions.question: The one-sentence justification an examiner rewards is:
options: 'The median, because it is the easiest to calculate'
'The mean, because it is the most famous measure'
'The median, because the data contains an outlier which distorts the mean'
'The mode, because the data are numbers'

questions.question: Everyone in a bucket is treated as sitting at its midpoint because:
options: The midpoint is always the mode
The exact values are hidden, and the middle is the fairest balanced guess

questions.question: Counting through buckets of 4, 6, 11, 12 and 7 learners, the 20th and 21st learners in mark order stand in:
options: The fifties bucket — the running count reaches 10, then 21

questions.question: The modal interval is found by pointing at:
options: The bucket with the most learners in it
The bucket with the widest interval
